facts.statement: Pahasapasaurus is distinguished by its elongated epipodial bones in the forelimbs and hindlimbs and by the specific structure of its palate bones.
facts.quote: Distinctive features of the taxon include elongate epipodial bones (radius/ulna - tibia/fibula) and the nature of the palate bones (roof of the mouth).

facts.statement: Bruce Schumacher formally named the species Pahasapasaurus haasi in 2007 based on a partial skeleton with a skull and lower jaws.
facts.quote: In 2007, Schumacher named Pahasapasaurus haasi, establishing AMM 98.1.1, a partial skeleton with skull and lower jaws, as the holotype.

facts.statement: The genus name Pahasapasaurus is derived from the Sioux language, meaning "Black Hills".
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Paha Sapa, meaning "Black Hills" in the Sioux language.

facts.statement: The specific name haasi honors Charles Christian Haas, the discoverer of the fossil.
facts.quote: The specific name honours C.C. Haas as discoverer.

facts.statement: The type species Pahasapasaurus haasi lived during the late Cenomanian age in the Greenhorn Limestone of South Dakota.
facts.quote: Pahasapasaurus haasi, was named in 2007 based on remains from the late Cenomanian-aged Greenhorn Limestone of South Dakota

facts.statement: A second species, Pahasapasaurus gillettei, lived during the early Turonian age in the Tropic Shale of Utah.
facts.quote: In 2025, a second species was named, Pahasapasaurus gillettei, based on a complete skull and partial skeleton from the early Turonian-aged Tropic Shale of Utah.

facts.statement: Pahasapasaurus belongs to the family Polycotylidae.
Pahasapasaurus lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Pahasapasaurus is an extinct genus of polycotylid plesiosaurs found in Late Cretaceous rocks in the United States.
rejected.quote: Pahasapasaurus is an extinct genus of polycotylid plesiosaurs from Late Cretaceous rocks of the United States.
